sources: Evans-Wentz, W. Y. The Fairy-Faith in Celtic Countries. Gerrards Cross: Colin Smythe Humanities Press, 1911, 220.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The puck is a British folkloric figure. The most famous is Puck, or Robin Goodfellow, of A Midsummer Night's Dream. Country dwellers knew the puck as a kind of pooka. It was a ghostly presence that caused mischief wherever it went. The puck is a small good-natured creature that lives to make trouble. It leads travelers astray and pushes furniture about. It can be induced to assist with farm labor when no reward is offered. Under the name Robin Goodfellow it appears as a half-human being. Some motifs trace back to the fairy king Manannán mac Lir.

okr.objective: Describe the puck as a mischievous British fairy.
